study type: Observational descriptive study / Retrospective review of autopsy cases
cohort: The study included organs from 65 maternal autopsies performed at a tertiary care hospital.
finding: Puerperal sepsis was the most frequent cause of maternal death (26.15%), followed by postpartum haemorrhage (21.54%) and Toxaemia of pregnancy (20%).
cross-section timing: Cases collected from January 1, 2016, to June 30, 2020
